learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the 'Rules of the Game'! Learn the fundamental principles, concepts, and assumptions that all accountants follow to keep reports consistent.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The business and its owner are TWO SEPARATE people in the eyes of accounting. That is why money taken by the owner for personal use is treated as 'Drawings' and reduces the capital.
We assume the business will run forever. Because of this, we don't record fixed assets at their selling price today, but rather at their original cost minus depreciation.
Under Cash basis, we record income only when cash is received. Under Accrual basis (the standard way), we record income when it is EARNED, whether the cash is received right now or later.

The rule is: 'Do not anticipate a profit, but provide for all possible losses.' If you think you might lose money, record it immediately. If you think you might make a profit, wait until it actually happens!

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Two-Sided Coin
fun_activity.instructions: The 'Dual Aspect Concept' says every transaction has two effects. Buy a chocolate for ₹50. Effect 1: A chocolate (Asset) comes to you. Effect 2: Cash (Asset) goes away. Try finding the two effects for everything you do today!

exam_tips: 📌 The fundamental accounting assumptions are: Going Concern, Consistency, and Accrual. Memorize these three!
📌 The Dual Aspect Concept is the entire foundation of the Double Entry System (Assets = Liabilities + Capital).
📌 'Closing stock is valued at cost or net realizable value, whichever is lower'—this is a direct application of the Prudence (Conservatism) principle.
quick_recap: ⭐ GAAP ensures uniformity and consistency in accounting records.
⭐ The Matching Concept ensures that expenses incurred to earn revenue are recognized in the same accounting period.
⭐ Accrual accounting provides a more accurate picture of a company's profitability than cash accounting.
